title: In 2029, a 375-Meter Asteroid Will Pass Closer Than Our Satellites

scenes.text: In 2029, an asteroid will pass closer to Earth than many of our satellites.
It's called Apophis, about three hundred seventy-five meters wide.
On April 13th, 2029, it passes within thirty-two thousand kilometers of Earth.
That's inside the orbit of the satellites that relay TV and weather.
You'll see it with your own eyes from parts of Europe, Africa and Asia.
And no, it won't hit us. Radar ruled out an impact for a hundred years. Close enough to see, far enough to relax.

description:
On April 13th, 2029, the asteroid Apophis will pass within 32,000 km of Earth, closer than geostationary satellites.
It should be visible to the naked eye from parts of Europe, Africa and Asia, and radar has ruled out an impact for at least 100 years.
Will you go out and look?
first_comment: Where will you watch Apophis from in 2029?
